title: Microburst rollforward playbook + KPI notebook
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, runbook-style playbook for a small-scale, controlled launch pattern were piloting internally: the "microburst". Microbursts are short-duration, semi-predictable traffic ramps for early feature validation where we intentionally push demand in bounded slices to validate latency/cost/eval signals without fully exposing production.

Audience and scope:
- Product Ops, Hosting SRE, Serving Runtime owners, Solutions Eng on standby.
- Applies to hosted API feature flags, and dedicated/dedicated-burst lanes. Not for full GA.

Goals (what success looks like for a microburst):
- Healthy 95th latency under SLO for 90% of requests during the burst (goal: 200ms for small prompt workloads).
- No automated rollback triggered by model-quality regressions (rolling eval pass rate >= 98%).
- Cost per 1k tokens within 15% of baseline for the controlled sample.
- Clear signal capture: top 3 user-facing errors and top 3 response-quality regressions are identified within 2 hours post-burst.

Key KPIs and signal thresholds (operational definitions):
- p50/p95 latency (ms): green < 120 / < 250, amber 120-200 / 250-400, red > 200 / > 400. Owner: eng-sre.
- Token cost per 1k: green < baseline*1.15, amber 1.15-1.35, red > 1.35. Owner: product-ops finance liaison.
- Inference error rate (5xx and serving timeouts): green < 0.2%, amber 0.2-1%, red > 1%. Owner: serving-runtime.
- Eval regression rate (automated eval against canary prompt set): green >= 98%, amber 95-98%, red < 95%. Owner: applied-ml.
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV cache): target >= 18% for the profile. Owner: serving-runtime.

Pre-burst checklist (must pass all):
- [ ] Canary model pinned and verified (model hash, quantization profile noted). Reference: JIRA:POPS-1127/PR-489.
- [ ] Dedicated lane capacity reserved for window (if using dedicated): confirm GPU pool size and burst policy. Contact: infra-duty.
- [ ] Traffic shaping script prepared and smoke-tested in staging (script id and args).
- [ ] Observability hooks verified: per-route trace sampling, token-level cost breakdown, and eval pipeline ingestion.
- [ ] On-call rota set for 3-hour window + 2 hours post analysis (eng-sre, applied-ml, product-ops).
- [ ] Stakeholder readout template pre-filled (time, owners, rollback conditions).

Microburst traffic pattern (example):
1) Warmup 0-10 minutes: low ramp (10rps) to populate KV cache and warm kernels.
2) Pulse 10-40 minutes: target slice (40rps) sustained for 30m.
3) Cooldown 40-55 minutes: step down to 15rps for cleanup and trace correlation.
4) Quiet 55-120 minutes: monitor at baseline.

Real-time runbook (if amber/red triggers):
- Amber: notify product-ops channel, hold additional bursts. Start deeper trace collection for next 30m. Owner: eng-sre.
- Red latency or 5xx spike: initiate immediate traffic reduction by 50% and kick automatic fallback to cheaper-compatible model variant for 10 minutes. If unresolved, full rollback of rollout flag. Owner: serving-runtime + product-ops.
- Red eval regression: pause burst program, flag for applied-ml triage, revert model version in the canary lane. Owner: applied-ml.
- Cost overshoot (red): throttle non-essential background work (async embeddings, offline batch jobs) and notify finance liaison.

Post-burst quick analysis (first 2 hours):
- Collect: raw traces, per-token cost logs, eval results, top 20 sampled responses, user error traces.
- Run: compare canary prompt-set eval against baseline, compute A/B delta and confidence intervals.
- Triage: assign the top 3 issues with owners and ETA for fix or mitigation.

Weekly KPI tracker (sample entries — fill after each microburst):
- 2025-01-15 | Burst#1 | p50=85ms p95=210ms | error=0.18% | eval=99.1% | cost delta +8% | status: green
- 2025-01-29 | Burst#2 | p50=95ms p95=320ms | error=0.9% | eval=97.2% | cost delta +22% | status: amber (cost), follow-ups: investigate batch sizing and quantization profile
- 2025-02-05 | Burst#3 | p50=88ms p95=175ms | error=0.11% | eval=98.9% | cost delta +6% | status: green

Open questions / hypotheses to test in next bursts:
- Does increasing KV cache TTL by 30s improve p95 more than it increases memory pressure? (owner: serving-runtime)
- Can we reduce cost delta by switching specific prompt families to 8-bit quantized variants without affecting eval pass rates? (owner: applied-ml)
- Network tail contributions: are a small fraction of regions responsible for p95 spikes? Add region-level slicing next run. (owner: infra)

Quick snippets / shorthand for the team (notes to self):
- If cache-hit ratio < 12% during warmup, consider pre-warming with golden prompts.
- If we see >2% 5xx in first 5 minutes, kill burst immediately and capture complete core dumps.
- Always tag bursts with BURST_ID and MODEL_HASH in observability to simplify join queries.

Stakeholder readout template (one-paragraph to paste into Slack/confluence):
- "Burst <BURST_ID> ran on <DATE>. Outcome: latency p95 <value>, automated eval pass rate <value>. Top action items: 1) <owner> to investigate <issue>, ETA <date>; 2) <owner> to adjust capacity/burst policy; 3) follow-up deep-dive scheduled <date>. Full log: <link>."

Appendix: quick links and artifact ids
- Canonical canary prompt set: CONFLUENCE:CANARY-PROMPTS-2025
- Burst orchestration job: infra/recipes/microburst-runner (PR-489)
- Cost analysis notebook: gs://redwood-dashboards/microburst/cost-2025q1.ipynb

Notes on doc provenance:
- Drafted during product-ops week-of 2025-01-06. Iterated with eng-sre on 2025-01-10 and applied-ml on 2025-01-22. Planning to convert to a templated playbook once 3 successful microbursts complete.

-- Lena (product-ops)
